387	true reality of the Jew, even as a soul in a body below,

391	Ah, the reality
392	that is certainly the main and true one. There is "main" in the
393	tangible sense, where one could say that the more
394	prominent reality is the reality of the matter, of the body, since that is
395	what one senses and feels in the physical world, yes.
396	But the main and true reality, even when he is
397	a soul in a body below, is his Divine soul, which is
398	truly a part of Elokah from above. So of course, compared to this, nothing
399	takes up any space. Compared to the fact that within me is a part
400	of Elokah from above, what can take up space? So it is clear
401	that this is the main thing, yes, this is the main and true thing. All the rest
402	is a reality that is created, something from absolute nothingness.
403	Then he says, in the well-known language, that not only is the soul
404	truly a part of Elokah from above, as is stated in the Zohar,
405	which repeats this many times, Israel and the Holy One, Blessed Be He,
406	are one: each Jew is one thing with
407	HaShem, blessed be He.
408	This is how the Rebbe opened the passage: this is the main
409	and true reality also of the soul in a body below.
410	That is, even when a Jew is a soul inside a body,
411	he is still one thing with the Holy One, Blessed Be He, in every
412	situation he is in, he is bound and connected with the Holy One, Blessed
413	Be He, and therefore he must be found also in the body before
414	HaShem your Elokim. So that the Jew in fact understands
415	the true order of importance of things, and how even
416	his soul in the body has not lost its true merit and
417	advantage, that it is one thing with the Holy One, Blessed
418	Be He. Consequently, where is the natural and simple place
419	where a Jew should be placed? Before
